title: Recovering Alice's bit from a disjoint coordinate
statement: Let $x, y \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a pair of bits that are not both $\mathrm{true}$. Then the disjoint coordinate built from $(x, y)$ has Alice's bit equal to $x$; that is, extracting Alice's bit from this coordinate returns $x$ exactly.
hypotheses_covered: x and y are not both true
replaced: \texttt{coordinateOfBits} preserves Alice's bit when the requested pair is disjoint.
